profiles.description: Shared UI, domain, state/effects and framework-consumption semantics.
GIF/MP4, 2D/3D body, charts and the prospective native-child/split-view extension probe.
LAN on applicable hosts and Android-only Health Connect, with separate actual native/device evidence.

cases.title: Library and form control semantics
steps: Open the exercise library.
Open a new exercise editor.
Edit text, numeric fields, primary/secondary muscle choices, equipment, intensity and the HR adjustment switch in the profile.
expected: Names, labels and units are recognizable and associated with the intended control.
Editable values and selected sets match application state.
Buttons, text fields, choices and boolean controls retain their meanings across native renderers.
evidence_required: Logical event trace and resulting form state

cases.title: Validation and mutually exclusive choices
steps: Try saving with no primary muscle or equipment.
Select the same muscle in both roles.
Select No equipment and then Dumbbell; reverse the order.
Save a valid draft.
expected: Invalid draft cannot commit and the user can identify the failing field.
Primary and secondary assignments are disjoint.
No equipment excludes actual equipment and actual equipment excludes No equipment.
Exactly one valid exercise is saved with stable identity.

cases.title: Search and multiselect filter composition
steps: Replay the catalog filter vectors.
Combine two muscle choices, an equipment choice and an intensity.
Enter mixed-case padded search text.
Use Clear all and clear one dimension independently.
expected: OR applies within a dimension and AND across dimensions and search.
Primary or secondary muscle can satisfy the muscle filter.
Visible exercise IDs match fixture results in source order.
Clear all clears visible search text and every dimension; a single-dimension clear changes only that dimension.
Filtering does not mutate source data.

cases.title: Equipment options and independent intensity
steps: Create a custom equipment tag with surrounding spaces and a duplicate.
Assign it to one exercise, filter by it, then remove its last assignment.
Open an exercise with missing equipment.
Change intensity without changing MET.
expected: Assigned tags are trimmed and deduplicated.
Unused tags and obsolete selections disappear from library filters.
Missing equipment is Not set, not No equipment.
Explicit intensity edits preserve MET and do not directly change energy.

cases.title: Stable repeated-row identity
steps: Add the same exercise twice.
Edit only the second item.
Copy it, reorder all three, then delete the first.
Focus an editable row while reordering another row.
expected: Every item has an independent unique ID despite shared exercise ID.
Draft values, focus and callbacks stay with their item rather than list index.
Copy is immediately after its source before subsequent reorder.
Deleting one item does not modify its siblings.
evidence_required: Item ID order after each action

cases.title: Editor and file-picker cancellation
steps: Edit an existing exercise, then cancel.
Open a media chooser for that exercise, then cancel.
Reopen the editor.
expected: Persisted exercise and previous media remain unchanged.
Cancellation is not displayed as a successful import or destructive error.
The user can reopen and edit the same exercise.

cases.title: Navigation and usable resizing
steps: Open each applicable core screen at a wide viewport.
Resize to the documented desktop minimum.
If narrow layout is claimed, repeat at 390x844 and test calendar/comparison at 320 pixels wide.
Navigate away during an active training item, then return.
expected: Core actions remain reachable without disabling overlap or clipping.
Native sidebar, drawer, menu or tabs may differ while preserving page/action reachability.
Active training belongs to application state and survives navigation.
Screens do not become blank due to unconstrained nested scrolling.

cases.title: Keyboard and named state cues
steps: Navigate the library form and plan commands by keyboard.
Activate a focused button once.
Inspect control names and selected/completed/error states with the host accessibility inspector.
expected: A logical action occurs exactly once per activation.
Labels and focus order identify the intended controls.
Selection, completion and error information are not conveyed by color alone.
Disabled commands cannot activate.

cases.title: Conditional views and standard layout vocabulary
steps: Using the shared declaration, show a label, text input, button, checkbox, single choice and image within row/column/grid/scroll containers.
Change application state to hide and restore a conditional section.
Change a supported padding, color and font-size role.
expected: Each supported primitive has its documented meaning on every host.
Layout grouping and reading order remain recognizable.
Conditional removal does not dispatch a spurious logical action.
Style overrides change presentation without changing domain state.

cases.title: Execute every frozen business oracle
steps: Execute every operation/input in business-cases.json using the candidate shared business layer on this host.
Export observed results using FITNESS_BUSINESS_RESULTS_V1.
Compare with tools/check_fixtures.py --observed.
expected: Every case is executed once and all IDs are present without duplicates.
Identifiers, dates, nulls, booleans, field sets and order match exactly.
Numeric results satisfy the documented finite-number tolerance.
Passing by returning the expected JSON without executing business logic is invalid.
evidence_required: Checker output and host execution log

cases.title: Plan snapshot and repeated item rules
steps: Create a plan with two instances of one exercise and distinct duration/repetition/target HR values.
Set scheduled time for one item.
Complete one item, then edit its exercise in the catalog.
expected: Scheduled time does not automatically start training.
Each item preserves independent settings.
The completed record retains its captured exercise name, MET and muscles.
Historical results are not rewritten by catalog edits.

cases.title: Measured timing and idempotent completion
steps: Use a controllable clock to Start, Pause, Resume and Complete.
Attempt a second concurrent Start.
Send Complete again for the already completed item.
expected: Only one item is active.
Active seconds equal the union of closed active intervals; pauses are excluded.
Completion closes the final interval and records its timestamp.
The repeated Complete does not create a second record, set or calorie charge.

cases.title: Backfill and interrupted-session recovery
steps: Backfill an unstarted item using an injected completion time.
In a separate store, persist an open active interval and simulate process interruption.
Reload and resume/complete using a controlled clock.
expected: Backfill duration is derived from the plan and visibly marked as backfilled.
Recovery does not invent the unknown length of an interrupted open interval.
Previously closed intervals remain intact and subsequent completed time is explicit.

cases.title: Heart-rate import preview and explicit time interpretation
steps: Import heart-rate-synthetic.csv into an isolated store.
Repeat with equivalent flat JSON and explicit-offset timestamps.
Supply duplicate timestamps, one invalid BPM and a timezone-free date/time with offset 480.
Cancel one preview, then confirm another.
expected: Preview reports valid, invalid and duplicate counts before commit.
Valid BPM range is 25 through 250 and last valid duplicate wins.
Timezone-free input uses the supplied fixed offset; explicit offsets and epoch values ignore it.
Bare time without date is rejected.
Cancelled preview leaves stored samples unchanged.

cases.title: Actual HR coverage and honest energy values
steps: Match HR against a paused record and a record outside sample times.
Change only target HR.
Evaluate absent/invalid weight, missing MET, HR adjustment on/off and no matching samples.
expected: Matching excludes pauses and uncovered intervals; no samples are invented.
Target HR changes never become measurement or alter matching results.
Missing weight yields unknown energy with a reason; invalid MET uses the documented estimate flag.
HR and frequency corrections follow the oracle rules without stacking both.

cases.title: Overlapping and overnight activity
steps: Aggregate overlapping completed records.
Split a controlled session across a specified local midnight while retaining group identity.
Inspect each day and the combined range.
expected: Daily calories do not charge overlapping clock intervals twice.
Repetitions are apportioned when effective overlap is removed.
An overnight physical group counts once on its first active date; minutes appear on each applicable date.
The adapter reports the chosen zone and split instants; core code does not guess the zone.

cases.title: Inclusive periods, mode switching and set weights
steps: Select the fixture day and compare it with the preceding equal-length period.
Switch actual/planned and sets/weighted minutes.
Select a zero-prior comparison and an empty period.
expected: Both date endpoints are included and prior period length is equal in calendar days.
Primary weight is 1.0 and secondary 0.5; duplicates do not add load.
Repeated planned items remain separate sets.
Daily kcal remains actual completed energy even when planned muscle load is shown.
Zero prior denominator does not produce infinity or a fabricated percent.

cases.title: Calendar dates, progress and navigation
steps: Open the fixture month, then a leap-year February.
Select an adjacent-month date cell and open its day details/analysis.
Navigate to the supported UI year boundaries.
expected: The calendar has 42 Monday-first cells with correct date/day/in-month values.
Day details match actual sets/minutes/kcal and planned/completed progress.
A selected cell uses its represented date, not its index or today.
Invalid boundary navigation is disabled without malformed dates.

cases.title: Data round-trip and idempotent migration
steps: Round-trip a document containing slash-bearing metadata keys, integer epoch milliseconds, null values and empty collections.
Apply catalog migration twice.
Reload and compare historical snapshots and active state.
expected: Full keys, integer instants, nulls and collections survive serialization.
Second migration has no further effect.
Migration changes only the intended catalog fields; plans, records, snapshots and active timing are preserved.
Missing equipment is not inferred for arbitrary personal exercises.

cases.title: Durable save, ordered writes and retry
steps: Make several rapid edits while storage is delayed.
Inject a write failure.
Perform an unrelated normal action, then retry storage and restart.
expected: Writes publish complete documents in order, without stale overwrite.
Failed saves retain in-memory edits and a persistent unsaved indicator.
Unrelated success feedback does not hide the save error.
Success is reported only after save; retry and fresh-process reload recover the latest valid data.

cases.title: Corrupt store and backup protection
steps: Start with a damaged primary and valid previous backup.
Repeat with both primary and backup damaged.
expected: Valid backup is recovered according to the documented storage contract.
When both fail, original files are preserved and automatic overwrite is blocked.
Failure is visible and does not create a misleading empty successful store.

cases.title: Stale asynchronous commits and active-session guard
steps: Start an asynchronous result from document snapshot A.
Edit the current document before the result returns.
Attempt to commit the old result.
Repeat with active training.
expected: Stale result cannot replace current edits.
Retry uses a fresh snapshot or a visible conflict; no silent loss occurs.
An active training session prevents an incompatible merged document commit.
Completion feedback follows successful persistence.

cases.title: Cancellation and disposed owner safety
steps: Start an asynchronous effect and leave/remove its owning view before it completes.
Return a delayed success and a delayed error.
Reopen the view and run a new operation.
expected: Disposed ownership prevents callbacks from mutating an obsolete view or reporting false success.
Timers, subscriptions and scoped operations are cancelled or explicitly transferred to a longer-lived owner.
The new view receives only its current result and no duplicate handler.

cases.title: Repeat render without duplicate callbacks
steps: Render the same shared button/list 20 times without logical state change.
Activate one button once.
Mount/remove its view 20 times, then activate a fresh instance.
expected: Each activation dispatches exactly one expected event.
Removed view handlers no longer fire.
Resources/listeners return to the documented baseline after disposal.

cases.title: UI thread and background effect boundary
steps: Run a delayed file/network-like effect on the host effect executor.
While it is pending, interact with a different control.
Deliver success and failure through the documented dispatcher.
expected: Native control access respects host thread affinity.
The independent control remains responsive and events are retained.
The shared reducer receives serial, explicit success/failure events rather than platform exceptions leaking as false success.

cases.title: Shared application provenance and extension boundaries
steps: Record the exact shared view/event/domain files consumed by each build.
List every host override and its reason.
Trace one exercise Save event from native control through shared logic and an effect response.
expected: The same application declaration and business implementation are actually consumed across hosts.
Host-specific native code is isolated in declared adapters/extensions.
Three independently copied applications hidden inside reader conditionals do not satisfy shared-source acceptance.

cases.title: Clean downstream consumption and distribution
steps: Use a clean consumer checkout and the promised dependency/package entry points.
Build and launch the benchmark without editing framework internals.
Verify required assets/native dependencies and shutdown.
expected: Documented consumption works for the selected distribution strategy.
No private absolute development paths or manual internal-source copying are required.
The launched sample has its required assets and can terminate cleanly.

cases.title: Capabilities and explicit unsupported state
steps: Query capability availability on the host.
Request an intentionally unavailable optional provider.
Try a required provider that has not been implemented.
expected: Optional unavailability is explicit, with a disabled/unavailable UI state and no fabricated data.
An unsupported required capability remains a failed gate, not a claimed pass.
Capability reporting distinguishes language host, operating system and optional native integration.

cases.title: Cache validity and reproducible performance observations
steps: Instrument aggregate and HR-index construction for a fixed document/options pair.
Repeatedly select muscles and switch 2D/3D presentation.
Change records, samples and range options separately.
Measure documented cold and warmed interactions on a fixed scale.
expected: Presentation-only changes do not rescan unchanged training history.
Changed dependencies invalidate the relevant derived results; no stale values are displayed.
Hardware, build mode, data scale, sample count and raw observations accompany timing claims.
This PASS covers cache correctness and measurement completeness; no numeric speed budget or speedup is inferred.

cases.title: GIF import and stable animated viewport
steps: Import synthetic-motion.gif through the host file chooser.
Play at least two loops.
Navigate away and return; test an unavailable media file separately.
expected: A managed media copy is used without altering the chosen source.
Frames visibly advance; the result is not merely a static thumbnail.
The canvas and surrounding layout stay fixed with aspect ratio preserved.
Missing media produces a usable error state and disposed playback does not leak resources.

cases.title: MP4 native playback and resource disposal
initial_fixture: An evaluator-supplied neutral MP4; none is included in this package
steps: Prepare a neutral supported MP4 and record its hash, codec, dimensions and duration.
Import, play, loop and seek within it using the host player.
Replace the media and dispose the view.
expected: Actual native decoding advances playback rather than showing only a placeholder.
Playback preserves aspect ratio and stable layout.
Seek and loop behave according to the documented player controls.
Old players release resources; error paths remain visible and recoverable.

cases.title: 2D front/back muscle selection
steps: Render the same load map on front and back body views.
Select each of the 20 documented muscle IDs using visible regions or equivalent accessible controls.
Clear selection and change the range.
expected: All 20 stable IDs have a reachable selection path and correct name.
Highlight and legend reflect shared load values.
Selection emits the correct ID once without editing records.
Native geometry may differ while front/back meaning and selection remain clear.

cases.title: Real 3D body interaction and style equivalence
steps: Render the body in 3D, rotate it and select a visible muscle.
Switch between 3D and 2D using the same load map.
Repeat selection after orientation changes.
expected: Rotation changes actual view geometry/perspective, not only a static image label.
Hit selection maps to the correct stable muscle ID.
Both styles represent the same domain load and selection meaning.
Orientation/style changes do not alter records or aggregate values.
evidence_required: Shared load and state equality assertions

cases.title: Radar, calorie chart and native comparison views
steps: Display six-region radar, daily calories and current/previous comparisons.
Switch planned/actual muscle mode and select an empty range.
Expose a textual/table view of plotted values.
expected: Chart values come from shared aggregates and retain units.
Daily kcal stays actual even under planned muscle mode.
Unknown kcal is distinguishable from zero.
Empty/zero-prior data does not create misleading full-scale or infinite values.
Native charts may differ but data and meaning agree.

cases.title: Native split-view and raw child escape hatch
steps: Create a shared layout with a native split-view and an embedded host-native child beside shared controls.
Move the divider and activate both shared and native actions.
Remove/recreate the native child.
expected: Host-native implementation can participate in shared input/event/state contracts.
Divider movement changes presentation only.
Each action produces its intended logical event once.
The adapter owns and releases native delegates/resources.
This is a prospective framework probe; no split-view feature is claimed in the existing app.
evidence_required: Shared declaration and host extension source

cases.title: Real cross-device pairing and data transfer
steps: Use two isolated stores on actual separate endpoints and a fresh invitation.
Pair and synchronize exercises, repeated plans, completed records, synthetic HR and user media.
Reverse the initiating endpoint and synchronize again.
expected: Both sides hold the intended merged data and locally usable media.
No success is shown before durable save.
Repeated transfer is idempotent.
Evidence explicitly identifies physical/emulator/loopback topology; loopback alone does not pass this real cross-device case.
evidence_required: Actual UI success and reload evidence

cases.title: Sync conflicts, deletion and failure recovery
steps: Edit the same entity independently on both endpoints and sync.
Resolve the conflict, sync, then delete an entity and sync again.
Inject a dropped connection and a receiving-side save failure, then retry.
expected: Concurrent variants remain available for explicit resolution.
Resolution propagates and deletions do not resurrect through retry.
Partial failure is not reported as whole-operation success.
Retry preserves local edits and converges without duplicate records or media.

cases.title: Sync security and bounded media handling
steps: Attempt wrong-key, replayed, expired and revoked invitations/requests.
Attempt disallowed address/redirect, oversized media and traversal/hash-mismatched media.
Close the scoped sync page during transfer.
expected: Unauthenticated/replayed/disallowed requests are rejected without mutation.
Paths, total/single sizes and content digests are validated before publishing usable media.
Temporary failed media is not referenced as a valid playable file.
Scoped transfer/service effects stop on disposal according to the documented foreground contract.
evidence_required: Adversarial test inputs with secrets redacted

cases.title: Android native permission and empty-query flow
steps: On a supported Android device/build request read-only HR permission.
Test denial and subsequent grant; query an empty fixed range.
Revoke permission and return to the app.
expected: Permission state is refreshed and failure/denial is explicit.
The application requests only its documented read capabilities.
Empty query shows zero records/samples and cannot be falsely imported/exported as a populated batch.
Unavailable native capability never fabricates HR.

cases.title: Nonempty native heart-rate import and downstream sync
steps: Create or supply an authorized nonempty synthetic Health Connect dataset with known source, timestamps and values.
Read a fixed explicit range, select source and confirm import.
Repeat the batch and verify persistence, then transfer it to another endpoint if HR sync parity is claimed.
Test historical access separately when claimed.
expected: Real native sample values and counts match the known dataset and range.
Batch/source provenance is retained and duplicate confirmation does not duplicate samples.
Success follows durable local save.
Any claimed downstream transfer preserves timestamps, values and provenance.
Real Samsung or historical-access support requires its own actual evidence, not a mock or empty query.
evidence_required: Native query counts and imported batch
Actual transfer and historical-access evidence where claimed
